title: MP-260024, UPlaNS N15 Jona – Échangeur de Reichenburg Auteur du projet – Planification du trafic Phases EK à IBN (NSG) // Phases 31 à 53 (SIA)
description:
Le tronçon UPlaNS N15/08, 10 Jona – échangeur de Reichenburg concerné par le projet présente des infrastructures d'âges différents.

 

Les derniers travaux de maintenance d’envergure, respectivement les derniers travaux d’aménagement partiel du tronçon, remontent à plus de 20 ans (Rapperswil-Jona–Schmerikon).

 

Le périmètre du projet comprend divers ouvrages d'art, notamment des passages inférieurs et supérieurs, des ouvrages de traversée, des murs de soutènement, des parois antibruit ainsi que des tunnels.

Compte tenu de l'âge avancé de la chaussée, un projet de maintenance est prévu pour ce tronçon.

 

Les principaux facteurs motivant ce projet sont ainsi l'évolution de l'état de la chaussée, des équipements d'exploitation et de sécurité (EES) et des différents ouvrages d'art, en particulier les tunnels, ainsi que la non-conformité aux normes du traitement des eaux de chaussée.

 

Les principales interventions prévues dans le cadre de ce projet de maintenance portent sur la remise en état des revêtements de chaussée, y compris les conduites d'évacuation des eaux, ainsi que de l'ensemble des ouvrages d'art et des tunnels (y compris les mesures visant à améliorer la sécurité du tunnel de Balmenrain), de même que sur le renouvellement complet des équipements d'exploitation et de sécurité (EES) dans le périmètre du projet.

 

Le mandat faisant l'objet du présent appel d'offres porte sur les prestations de planification du trafic pour les phases allant du concept global de maintenance (MK) jusqu'à la mise en service (MES) incluse.

buyer: Etat du Valais, Service immobilier et patrimoine - Investissements
title: Extension et rénovation du Lycée-collège de St-Maurice - CFC 4
description:
Le Lycée-Collège de Saint-Maurice accueille environ 1'100 élèves encadrés par une centaine d’enseignants. Fort d’une longue tradition éducative, ce lieu emblématique joue un rôle clé dans la formation gymnasiale du canton du Valais, et jouit d’une renommée confirmée.

L’établissement est réparti sur deux sites distincts :

  • le site du Lycée-Collège situé à proximité immédiate de la gare et de la vieille ville de Saint-Maurice ;
  • le site de la Zone sportive, voisin des installations sportives de la commune.

Ces deux sites sont distants d’un peu plus de 300 mètres, soit à environ cinq minutes à pied.

Le projet d’extension et de transformation du Lycée-Collège prévoit la construction, au nord-ouest du site, d’un nouveau pavillon en bois comprenant un sous-sol et quatre niveaux. Il inclut également la rénovation de l’Internat, propriété de l’Abbaye de Saint-Maurice, ainsi que la transformation du bâtiment existant en forme de H.

title: Équipe de planification générale pour le projet Sirius3 – Infrastructure commune de formation et de perfectionnement pour les sapeurs-pompiers, la protection civile et la police cantonale
description:
L'Assurcane immobilière Berne (AIB) et l’Amt für Grundstücke und Gebäude (AGG) réalisent conjointement le projet Sirius3 et procèdent, à cette fin, à l’acquisition des prestations d’une équipe de planification générale.

À la suite de l’étude de faisabilité et de l’évaluation des sites, le présent appel d’offres vise à sélectionner, pour les phases d’étude et de réalisation du projet Sirius3, une équipe de planificateurs placée sous la direction d’un planificateur général.

Conformément aux phases de prestations définies par la SIA, l’équipe de planification doit fournir l’ensemble des prestations nécessaires, depuis les études de projet jusqu’à la mise en service de l’ensemble du projet Sirius3. En fonction des décisions politiques et des décisions de financement, les différentes phases pourront être déclenchées et mandatées successivement.

La mission est exigeante et présente un degré élevé de complexité. De nombreux ouvrages spéciaux doivent être planifiés et réalisés sur un vaste site. Il s’agit notamment des installations suivantes :

  • Installation de formation des sapeurs-pompiers : l’installation d’entraînement permet aux sapeurs-pompiers de s’exercer, dans des conditions réelles, à la lutte contre les incendies, au sauvetage de personnes lors d’accidents, aux interventions techniques, y compris en cas d’incendie et de situations particulières, ainsi qu’aux interventions en cas d’accidents impliquant des hydrocarbures ou des substances ABC. L’enveloppe extérieure et les installations techniques du bâtiment doivent être conçues de manière à empêcher toute émission vers l’extérieur, notamment de chaleur, de fumées ou de substances chimiques. Dans l’installation d’entraînement, les participants s’exercent, équipés d’appareils de protection respiratoire, à l’extinction d’éléments de bâtiments, d’équipements et de véhicules en feu. Les causes d’incendie et les phénomènes liés au comportement du feu, tels que le flash-over, y sont également démontrés.
  • Stand de tir souterrain de 50 m, ainsi qu’un stand de tir de 100 m intégrant une installation de 30 m avec des dispositifs pare-balles sur trois côtés.
  • Village d’exercice : il sert d’installation d’entraînement pour l’acquisition de compétences policières spécifiques, telles que l’approche tactique d’un bâtiment et sa surveillance, la protection de personnes ou les interventions nocturnes. Différentes installations d’exercice sont disposées dans un espace extérieur. Elles comprennent notamment des bâtiments individuels de plusieurs étages avec cages d’escalier et balcons, des toitures inclinées et plates équipées de points de rappel, ainsi que des épaves de véhicules, telles que voitures particulières, tramways et autobus.
  • Infrastructures spéciales « Haut + Bas », décombres, bois et protection contre les eaux : ces installations permettent à la protection civile de s’exercer, dans des conditions réelles, au sauvetage de personnes ainsi qu’aux travaux de dégagement, de récupération et de déblaiement. Les installations reproduisent différents événements et situations de danger et sont équipées en conséquence. Le secteur de décombres avec galerie souterraine simule par exemple la situation après un séisme. Les ouvrages en hauteur et souterrains équipés de bassins d’inondation, ainsi que l’installation de simulation des crues, permettent quant à eux de reproduire des situations d’inondation ou les conséquences de chutes de pierres et de glissements de terrain.

En complément, différentes unités fonctionnelles nécessaires à l’exploitation du centre de formation doivent être réalisées, notamment des vestiaires, des zones de changement d’équipement, des locaux de stockage, un restaurant, des salles de formation, des salles plénières, un dojo et des locaux d’hébergement.

En raison de la grande complexité du projet et des exigences particulières en matière de planification et de coordination, les organes de projet compétents ont décidé d’assurer la qualité dans le cadre de la procédure d’adjudication. L’objectif est de pouvoir évaluer, outre les compétences professionnelles de l’équipe de planification, la qualité et l’adéquation des solutions proposées, afin de sélectionner le partenaire de planification le mieux adapté à cette mission exigeante.

Dans le cadre de l’étude d’idées, les équipes de planification retenues recevront les exigences spécifiques formulées par les différents groupes d’utilisateurs.

title: Procurement of a New ERP Solution
description:
The Centre for Laboratory Medicine (Zentrum für Labormedizin, ZLM), an independent public-law institution of the Canton of St. Gallen, is procuring an integrated ERP solution close to standard to replace its existing SAP solution and the ancillary system ProCommerce (purchasing and warehouse).


Subject of the procurement

  • Licences or rights of use for the standard software
  • Implementation of the solution at a fixed price (design, configuration, interfaces, data migration, testing, training, go-live on 1 January 2028)
  • Maintenance, further development and support for the duration of the contract


Functional scope

  • Order-to-cash: transfer of laboratory orders and services from the laboratory information systems, tariff application (including the Swiss Federal Office of Public Health's List of Analyses), invoicing, accounts receivable management and dunning
  • Accounts payable and purchasing (source-to-pay)
  • Warehouse and logistics, including batch and expiry date management
  • Financial accounting, fixed asset accounting and cost accounting, controlling and reporting in accordance with Swiss GAAP FER
  • Master data, interfaces (via the Mirth middleware) and migration
  • On-premises operation in the HOCH IT data centre, with the option of a later move to the cloud


Options (not evaluated): "Projects and project costs" and "Integrated web shop".


Not included: HR and payroll, CRM, laboratory information systems, sample logistics and waste disposal.

title: Switzerland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – (25002) 609 Swiss Government Cloud
description: The aim is to implement the Federal Administration's cloud strategy of 11 December 2020 (SB020 – Federal Cloud Strategy). To this end, this procurement is being carried out using the selective procedure in accordance with Article 19 of the PPA and is divided into three lots: * Lot 1: Public cloud – global reach (public cloud with global data storage) * Lot 2: Public cloud – enhanced data governance (public cloud with data storage and processing exclusively in Switzerland) * Lot 3: Private cloud – on premises (private cloud with data storage and processing exclusively at the requesting office's locations) In order to spread outage and security risks across several tenderers, increase security of supply and reduce dependence on individual tenderers, the requesting office is pursuing a multi-supplier strategy. A total of five awards will be made (two each for lots 1 and 2, and one for lot 3), each to a different tenderer, for the acquisition of the cloud services and related goods/services put out to tender here. To achieve this objective, a lot limitation within the meaning of Article 32 paragraph 3 of the PPA is provided for. Further information can be found in the tender documentation.

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

description: INTRODUCTION The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) anticipates soliciting proposals and subsequently awarding a single firm-fixed-price contract for the design-bid-build minor construction project #593-407, Diagnostic Imaging Center Expansion Minor Construction at VA Southern Nevada Healthcare System (VASNHS) located at 6900 North Pecos Rd., North Las Vegas, NV 89086. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The contractor shall provide all tools, equipment, materials, labor, supervision, and management to complete the construction of a new 2-story expansion and renovation to expand the Radiology Department and integrate with the Emergency Department. Construction practices shall comply with all VA solicitation drawings and specifications, VA regulations, procedures, and conditions for work at the medical center and any applicable codes as per requirements of all governing agencies. This project shall construct a new 2- story 11,282 square foot Diagnostic Imaging Center Expansion and renovate 870 square feet of an adjacent storage room and exam space in the Emergency Department to expand the Radiology Department and integrate the two spaces. The first floor will consist of a state-of-the-Art facility fully equipped for provisions or services to house (2) MRI, CT, X-ray, Ultrasound, Administrations and Support spaces to support the Radiology Department. The second floor will be an extension of the existing penthouse that services the Emergency Department. The project will include the relocation of existing utilities that encroach into the building footprint of the new expansion as shown on the design documents. Work includes general construction, alterations, and certain other items. Services include but not limited to furnish all supervision, labor, equipment, materials, and transportation necessary to accomplish work for the demolition and replacement as required by specifications and drawings. Contractor shall complete the intent of project 593-407 in strict accordance with the SOW, drawings, and specifications. All work not specifically identified by the drawings and/or specifications but necessary for a complete system shall be included as if specifically identified in the Contract Documents. ADMINISTRATIVE The solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposals (RFP) conducted in accordance with FAR part 15 and will be evaluated in accordance with the tradeoff procedures listed in the solicitation. The solicitation will be issued as a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) set-aside. Offers received from other than SDVOSB concerns will not be considered. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45.0 million. The solicitation will be issued in late Nov 2026. The period of performance is approximately 480 calendar days from the issuance of the notice to proceed. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. This notice is not a request for competitive offers. All questions must be submitted in writing to the issuing office via email to Jessica.stevenson3@va.gov. Telephone calls will not be accepted.

title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System
description: The Heat Pipe Reactor Fire Mitigation and Suppression System from Los Alamos National Laboratory, transforms the heat pipes inside an alkali metal-cooled nuclear reactor from passive thermal conduits into active, sensor-driven fire defense components, giving designers of advanced small and microreactors a layered, automated safeguard against one of the most challenging hazards in their systems. By combining an inert gas buffer, a phase change material jacket, automated suppressant injection at multiple points and optional neutron-absorber dispersion into the reactor core, the system delivers redundant protection that responds within milliseconds of detecting fire-like conditions. This system enables advanced reactor developers to meet stringent safety expectations for remote, unattended and space-constrained deployments without redesigning the core architecture around bulky external suppression equipment. How it Works During normal operation, each heat pipe carries thermal energy away from the reactor core through the evaporation and condensation of an alkali metal working fluid, while valves connecting the heat pipe to external suppressant chambers remain closed. Temperature and pressure sensors continuously monitor the heat pipe reactor core and the valves near each heat pipe end, feeding data to a controller that compares readings against predefined thresholds. When a reading crosses the first threshold, the controller opens a valve and forces a fire suppressant material, typically a boron compound, into the interior of the heat pipe. If conditions worsen and a second threshold is crossed, additional valves activate to inject suppressant from the opposite end of the heat pipe, evacuate the working fluid through a dedicated valve and release suppressant into an inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe at the heat exchanger interface. Technical Description The system architecture centers on a heat pipe reactor core engaging a plurality of dual-ended or single-ended heat pipes, where both ends of each heat pipe extend externally of the core block so that suppressant can be introduced from either side of the core. A heat exchanger device sits at the heat rejection end of each heat pipe and defines an enclosed inert gas chamber that annularly surrounds the heat pipe, creating a physical gap between the alkali metal working fluid and any water-based cooling fluid. The chamber adds a second point of failure that must occur before incompatible fluids can interact, and the inert gas itself can serve as a blanketing agent for active flames. A layer of phase change material, typically a salt that doubles as a Class D fire extinguishing agent and alkali metal fire retardant, is disposed on the outer surface of the gas chamber, partitioned by fin-bearing components that both store thermal energy and improve heat transfer to the surrounding cooling fluid. The active suppression and shutdown logic is governed by a controller comprising memory, processor, input/output circuitry and communications circuitry, optionally implemented as a distributed or cloud-based system. First and second valves regulate suppressant flow into each end of the heat pipe interior cavity from dedicated suppressant chambers, while third and fourth valves regulate suppressant flow into the inert gas chamber from separate chambers. The second valve at the heat pipe�s far end can also be configured to evacuate working fluid either simultaneously with or prior to suppressant injection, encouraging dispersion of the suppressant throughout the pipe. As an additional shutdown pathway, the reactor core block can include gaps between fuel rods and heat pipes in which a neutron absorber material such as cadmium or a boron compound is preloaded; on detection of an alkali metal fire, the controller can release that absorber into the gaps to reduce core reactivity and aid shutdown, providing a coupled fire-and-reactivity response unique to this design. Advantages Multiple independent barriers between reactive alkali metals and potential ignition sources, reducing the probability of a single-point failure Automated, sensor-driven response that opens valves and injects suppressant within milliseconds of fire-like conditions being detected Dual-purpose phase change jacket that stores thermal energy during normal operation and acts as a fire retardant during an event Coupled fire suppression and reactor shutdown through optional neutron absorber dispersion into the core Flexible architecture compatible with both heat pipe-cooled reactor cores and auxiliary equipment such as molten salt pumps Configurable suppressant choices and threshold logic, allowing developers to tailor the response to their specific reactor design Market Applications Nuclear Energy (microreactors, small modular reactors, heat pipe-cooled designs) Power Generation (remote bases, mining sites, Arctic installations) Space and Lunar Surface Power (radioisotope and fission surface power systems) Industrial Process Heat (high-temperature manufacturing, hydrogen production facilities) Marine and Naval Propulsion (advanced compact reactor concepts for maritime use) Nuclear Safety Instrumentation (sensor and controller subsystems for licensed reactor operators) Development Status: TRL 3 U.S. Patent No. 12,640,276 LA-UR-26-25100 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. title: Morphine Sulfate Solution
description: The Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is planning to issue a solicitation for a national requirements contract for Morphine Sulfate Solution. Procurement details follow. Morphine Sulfate 2MG/ML and 4MG/ML Injection Syringe and 2MG/ML and 10MG/ML Intravenous Syringe in Packs of 10. Morphine Sulfate 2MG/ML, 4MG/ML, and 10MG/ML Injection Solution Vial and 4MG/ML and 10MG/ML Intravenous Solution Vial in Boxes of 25. Competition will be restricted to domestic sources (vendors providing Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) and Final Dosage Forms (FDF) manufactured domestically), the procurement will be competed among all qualified domestic manufacturers. The contract will be a firm-fixed price, requirements type contract with a one-year base and four one-year options. A contract resulting from this solicitation will establish a national supply source, in accordance with FAR 52.216-21 (Requirements), to provide the items listed in the schedule for purchase by Department of War (DoW), Department of Veterans Affairs, Indian Health Service and Bureau of Prisons customers through the DLA and VA prime vendor programs. The annual usage estimates will be provided in the Schedule of Supplies section of the solicitation. This is a commercial item and will be solicited using FAR part 12. All sources may submit a proposal which shall be considered by the agency. A copy of the solicitation will be posted to the DLA Bid Board System (DIBBS) at https://www.dibbs.bsm.dla.mil and Sam.Gov at https://sam.gov/. Interested parties should contact Christopher Newman at (445) 737-7371 or Christopher.Nemwan@dla.mil with any questions/comments. Interested parties are further advised to set up automated notifications of pre-solicitation or solicitation changes through this website. The current projected solicitation date is October/November of 2026. DLA reserves the right to issue the solicitation before or after the projected solicitation date.

title: Belgium – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Flankerend onderzoeks- en evaluatieprogramma Loopbaankrediet
description: Dit bestek beschrijft het flankerend onderzoeks- en evaluatieprogramma van het stelsel van loopbaankrediet. Dat is het nieuwe stelsel van gesubsidieerde loopbaanbegeleiding dat vanaf 2027 door het Departement WEWIS wordt ingezet om professioneel actieve personen te ondersteunen en te versterken in hun loopbaan. Het stelsel van loopbaankrediet is de opvolger van het huidige stelsel van loopbaancheques. Het flankerend onderzoeks- en evaluatieprogramma heeft volgende doelstellingen: • Beoordelen in welke mate de hervormingsdoelstellingen van het stelsel van loopbaankrediet rond kwaliteit, efficiëntie en administratieve vereenvoudiging werden gerealiseerd • Beoordelen in welke mate gesubsidieerde loopbaanbegeleiding via het stelsel van loopbaankrediet bijdraagt aan positieve effecten bij de gebruikers op korte en middellange termijn • Identificeren van mogelijkheden voor verdere ontwikkeling en bijsturing van het stelsel van loopbaankrediet om de doeltreffendheid en doelmatigheid van het stelsel te versterken, op te volgen en te evalueren in de toekomst • Leren over de manieren waarop werknemers en zelfstandigen optimaal kunnen worden ondersteund in hun actieve loopbaan Om deze doelstellingen te realiseren identificeert de opdrachtgever vijf onderdelen: 1. Evalueerbaarheids- en inceptiestudie van loopbaanbeleid; 2. Procesevaluatie van het stelsel van loopbaankrediet; 3. Evaluatie van de doeltreffendheid van het stelsel van loopbaankrediet; 4. Ontwikkeling en testing van kader voor toekomstige beleidsmonitoring en evaluatie. 5. Activiteiten in functie van kennisdeling, disseminatie en validering

title: Czechia – Network equipment – Rozšíření a podpora DWDM
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je povinnost dodavatele dodat a následně implementovat technické a programové prostředky pro rozšíření stávajících DWDM zařízení a poskytovat k nim a ke stávajícím technickým a programovým prostředkům služby podpory. Bližší specifikace předmětu veřejné zakázky je uvedena v návrhu smlouvy, který tvoří přílohu č. 1 zadávací dokumentace. Vzhledem ke skutečnosti, že zadavatel má plně integrovány stávající HW a SW prostředky DWDM ve své IS struktuře a rozšíření přenosové kapacity mezi lokalitami o 100 Gb nelze z důvodu kompatibility provést jinak než za užití prostředků, které jsou předmětem této zakázky, a přechod na jiné HW a SW prostředky by s sebou nesl nepřiměřeně vysoké náklady na straně zadavatele, ať již při pořízení zcela nových DWDM zařízení (míněno i za stávající prostředky, u nichž výměna není potřebná), či při nezbytné úpravě všech stávajících aplikací a systémů, které tyto prostředky užívají, má zadavatel za to, že je v tomto případě odůvodněno samotným předmětem veřejné zakázky odkazování na konkrétní výrobek, resp. na HW a SW prostředky a podporu konkrétního výrobce, jehož pořízení je předmětem této veřejné zakázky. Zadavatel nepřistoupil k rozdělení veřejné zakázky na části, neboť předmět veřejné zakázky tvoří jeden funkční celek a je zadáván v časové souvislosti. Zadavatel je při zadání veřejné zakázky v postavení poskytovatele regulované služby, a to v režimu vyšších povinností ve smyslu zákona č. 264/2025 Sb., o kybernetické bezpečnosti, v platném znění, a jeho prováděcích předpisů, kdy tato skutečnost je zohledněna zadavatelem v zadávacích podmínkách této veřejné zakázky.

title: High Power Electromagnetics (HPEM) Modeling and Effects BAA
description: This is a five (5) year Closed One-Step BAA with CALLs that will be utilized to solicit proposals for the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL), Directed Energy Directorate (DE), High Power Electromagnetic Division (RDH), for research areas of interest for High Power Electromagnetics (HPEM) Modeling and Effects. This closed BAA approach allows for proposal submission at a specified date and time, which will be posted through the issuance of CALLs at various times against this BAA. As requirements within the technical topic areas are identified, CALLs will be issued in SAM.gov to request proposals for specific research efforts. Multiple subsequent CALLs are anticipated and may be announced sequentially or concurrently in SAM.gov. CALLs will be issued unrestricted. The Government reserves the right to re-issue previously announced CALL areas with a second, subsequent submittal period. The Government also reserves the right to issue no CALLs for any given technology area.

title: JYK 3 peruskorjaus projektinjohtourakka
description: JYK 3 peruskorjaus projektinjohtourakka Järvenpään kaupunki (jäljempänä ”Tilaaja”) pyytää tarjoustanne Järvenpään yhteiskoulun 3. vaiheen (JYK 3) peruskorjaushankkeen projektinjohtourakasta (PJU) tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Hankinnan kohteena on osoitteessa Kansakoulunkatu 1, 04400 Järvenpää sijaitsevan koulurakennuksen peruskorjaus. Vuonna 1952 valmistunut koulurakennus on asemakaavassa suojeltu merkinnällä sr-11. Peruskorjauksen laajuus on noin 4 063 brm². Hanke käsittää koulurakennuksen laajan peruskorjauksen, taloteknisen perusparannuksen, tilamuutokset sekä rakennukseen liittyvät piha- ja aluerakennustyöt. Peruskorjaus käsittää muun muassa: - rakennuksen sisäpuoliset purku-, korjaus- ja muutostyöt - rakennuksen rakenteiden, julkisivujen, ikkunoiden, ovien ja vesikaton korjaustyöt suunnitelmien mukaisessa laajuudessa - taloteknisten järjestelmien (LVIA ja sähkö) uudistamisen - tilojen pintarakenteiden, kiintokalusteiden ja varusteiden uusimisen sekä muutostyöt - piha-alueiden, kulkuyhteyksien ja aluerakenteiden muutostyöt. Urakka sisältää kaikki tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaiset rakennus-, purku-, maa- ja talotekniset työt tarvittavine oheistöineen siten, että rakennuskohde saatetaan täysin valmiiksi ja käyttötarkoitustaan vastaavaan kuntoon. Rakennuskohde sijaitsee koulutontilla, jolla on myös muita käytössä olevia koulurakennuksia. Niissä koulun toiminta jatkuu rakennustöiden aikana. Urakoitsijan tulee huomioida toiminnan jatkuminen erityisesti työmaajärjestelyissä, kulkuyhteyksissä, työmaan turvallisuudessa ja työstä aiheutuvien haittojen hallinnassa. Hankinta toteutetaan projektinjohtourakkana, joka muodostuu kehitysvaiheesta ja sen jälkeen tilaajan erillisellä päätöksellä käynnistettävästä toteutusvaiheesta. Kehitysvaiheessa valittu projektinjohtourakoitsija osallistuu yhteistyössä tilaajan ja suunnittelijoiden kanssa hankkeen suunnitelmien, toteutusratkaisujen, hankintojen, aikataulun ja kustannusten tarkentamiseen sekä toteutusvaiheen valmisteluun. Toteutusvaiheessa projektinjohtourakoitsija toimii kohteen pääurakoitsijana ja lainsäädännön tarkoittamana päätoteuttajana sekä vastaa työmaan johtovelvollisuuksista, työmaapalveluista ja hankintojen toteuttamisesta tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa määritellyssä laajuudessa. Toteutusvaiheen käynnistäminen edellyttää tilaajan erillistä päätöstä. Hankinnan kaupallinen malli, kehitys- ja toteutusvaiheen tehtävät sekä sopimusmenettely on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteissä. Projektinjohtourakan kehitysvaihe käynnistyy alustavasti helmikuussa 2027 hankintapäätöksen tekemisen, hankintalain mukaisen odotusajan ja kehitysvaiheen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisen jälkeen. Rakentamisvaiheen on tarkoitus käynnistyä maalis–huhtikuussa 2027. Tarkempi rakentamisen aloitusajankohta ja toteutusaikataulu sovitaan kehitysvaiheen aikana yhteistyössä tilaajan kanssa. Urakan tulee olla kokonaisuudessaan valmis ja tilaajan hyväksytysti vastaanottama viimeistään 1.12.2028. Kaikki rakennuksen käyttöönottoon, turvallisuuteen ja toiminnan aloittamiseen olennaisesti vaikuttavat virheet ja puutteet tulee olla korjattuina tähän määräaikaan mennessä. Mahdollisten vähäisten, käyttöönottoa estämättömien virheiden ja puutteiden korjaamisesta sovitaan erikseen tilaajan kanssa. Urakan hyväksytyn vastaanoton edellytyksenä on lisäksi rakennusvalvontaviranomaisen hyväksyntä rakennuksen käyttöönotolle osittaisessa loppukatselmuksessa (käyttöönottokatselmuksessa) tai loppukatselmuksessa siltä osin kuin hyväksynnän saaminen riippuu PJU:n vastuulla olevista suorituksista ja velvoitteista. PJU:n vastuualueen ulkopuolisesta syystä johtuva viranomaishyväksynnän viivästyminen ei yksin estä PJU:n urakkasuorituksen sopimusoikeudellista vastaanottoa, mikäli muut vastaanoton edellytykset täyttyvät. Tarkemmat ehdot on määritelty urakkaohjelmassa ja toteutusvaiheen sopimusluonnoksessa. Rakennuksen käyttäjien muutto ja toiminnan käynnistämiseen liittyvät järjestelyt ajoittuvat alustavasti joulukuulle 2028. Toiminta rakennuksessa on tarkoitus aloittaa tammikuussa 2029. Tarjoajille järjestetään mahdollisuus tutustua rakennuskohteeseen ja siellä vallitseviin olosuhteisiin kahtena ennalta ilmoitettuna ajankohtana: - torstaina 12.11.2026 klo 9-10.30 - keskiviikkona 18.11.2026 klo 9-10.30 Kohdetutustumisiin voi osallistua saapumalla paikalle edellä ilmoitettuina ajankohtina. Erillistä ilmoittautumista ei edellytetä. Kohteeseen tutustuminen on suositeltavaa, mutta ei tarjouksen jättämisen edellytys. Tarjoaja vastaa siitä, että se on perehtynyt hankkeen lähtötietoihin ja huomioinut tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoissa esitetyt olosuhteet ja vaatimukset tarjouksessaan. Tarjouspyyntöä koskevat kysymykset tulee esittää Tarjouspalvelun kautta tarjouspyynnössä ilmoitettuun määräaikaan mennessä. Kohdetutustumisten yhteydessä ei anneta tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoja täydentäviä tai muuttavia tietoja, vaan kaikki tällaiset tarkennukset toimitetaan tarjoajille Tarjouspalvelun kautta. Tarjoajan edellytetään tulkitsevan tarjouspyyntöasiakirjoja rakennusalan ammattilaisena ja asiantuntijana. Mikäli tarjoaja havaitsee asiakirjoissa puutteita tai epäselvyyksiä, jotka voivat vaikuttaa tarjouksen sisältöön, tulee niistä tiedustella tarjouspyynnössä esitetyllä tavalla ennen tarjouksen jättämistä. Urakan tarkempi sisältö, toteutusmalli, kaupalliset ehdot sekä sopimusasiakirjojen keskinäinen pätevyysjärjestys on määritelty tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.,

title: Fernwärme Wil, civil engineering TP11.01 Center South
description:
Technischen Betriebe Wil (Wil Municipal Utilities) are planning a district heating network supplied by waste heat from the ZAB waste incineration plant in Bazenheid. A transfer pipeline, approximately 5 km in length, will transport the heat to the southern part of the city of Wil. From there, it will be distributed to customers via two main pipelines: one extending westward to the St. Gallen Psychiatric Services facility, and the other eastward—passing the Lindenhof school complex—to the Wil Hospital.

This tender concerns civile engineering for sub-project 11.01, "Zentrum Süd" (Center South), which encompasses a section of the "West" main pipeline. The total length of the route to be constructed (excluding individual building connections) is approximately 800 meters.

The project also includes the renewal of gas and water pipelines.

As part of this project, the southern edge of the "Stadtmarkt" bus stop will be upgraded to ensure accessibility for persons with disabilities.

The construction work will also affect several traffic signal installations.

title: Exploratory Advanced Research (EAR) Program FY 2027 Data Science Solicitation
description: 693JJ327BAA0002 FORMERLY 693JJ326BAA0006 This BAA is an expression of interest only and does not commit the Government to pay any proposal preparation costs. All responsible sources capable of satisfying the Government's needs may submit a proposal. The Government reserves the right to award or to not award contracts or other instruments determined to be of benefit to the Government in achieving the goals of this program. The EAR Program addresses the need to conduct research on longer term and higher risk breakthrough topics with the potential for transformational improvements to plan, build, renew, and operate safe, congestion free, and environmentally sound transportation systems. The Program scans broadly for advances in science and engineering to identify research topics where FHWA investment has the potential to make a significant impact. The EAR Program has identified an Agency need for data science for highway transportation research with the following objectives: 1. Engage and expand the community of researchers interested in applying emerging and advanced data methods for highway transportation research. 2. Demonstrate potential of emerging and exploratory data analytic techniques for highway transportation.

title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to the attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Alicia Vesey, at alicia.m.vesey.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Paul Kang, at paul.k.kang.civ@us.navy.mil. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. These attachments will be transmitted via DoD SAFE. To receive access to Attachment J-2 (Work Item Plans, Drawings and Other References}, including references that contain limiting distribution statements, provide a written request to the Mid-Atlantic Regional Maintenance Center (MARMC) Technical Librarian, Timothy Russell at timothy.russell1.civ@us.navy.mil with a copy to the Contract Specialist and the Contracting Officer listed above. Include your company SAM UEI number with the request so that contractor status can be confirmed in the System for Award Management. title: Design/Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR), Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21, JBMDL, NJ
description: 10/08/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date, Solicitation Number as well as building description have been updated*** 08/30/2026: ***Anticipated Solicitation Date as well as building description has been updated*** ***THE SOLICITATION NUMBER HAS BEEN UPDATED TO W912QR27RA004*** DESCRIPTION: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Louisville District intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) W912QR27RA004 for the Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Area Maintenance Support Activity (AMSA) 21 at Joint Base McGuire-Dix-Lakehurst (JBMDL) in Burlington, New Jersey. The project will repair failing facility components and extend the economic life of the facility by 25 years, providing a modern maintenance facility that enables readiness for the Army Reserve units located in the surrounding area. The project scope includes the repair of the failing HVAC and electrical systems, the removal of non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspaces as required, the repair/replacement/upgrade of light fixtures with code compliant units, the installation of a code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, and the repair of electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. The project also repairs the exterior structural elements, replaces the failing standing seam metal roof, and corrects all life safety deficiencies while maintaining the elements of the building's exterior. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. All hazardous materials (HAZMAT) removed as part of the demolition will be disposed of following all state and federal guidelines. The Contract Duration is one thousand ninety-five (1,095) calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed. TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) for this effort is 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: This acquisition will be a 100%Total Small Business Set-Aside. SELECTION PROCESS: This will be a two-phase Design/Build procurement process. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best Value Tradeoff source selection process. Potential offerors are invited to submit their performance, technical, and capability information as will be described in section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. The selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors (not necessarily in order): Past Performance and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be invited to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, and Price. Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II are subject to change with the Phase II amendment.) All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the Government's best interest. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. ANTICIPATED SOLICITATION RELEASE DATE: The Government anticipates releasing the solicitation on or about 30 October 2026 and approximate closing date on or about 30 November 2026. Actual dates and times will be identified in the solicitation. Responses to this synopsis are not required. Additional details can be found in the solicitation when it is posted. This notice will be updated if the anticipated soliciation release date extends beyond 30 October 2026. SITE VISIT: A site visit will be held following the issuance of the Phase II solicitation to the Offerors selected to move forward. The exact location and time will be included in the solicitation. SOLICITATION WEBSITE: The official solicitation, when posted, will be available free of charge by electronic posting only and may be found at federal Contracting Opportunities website, https://sam.gov. Paper copies of the solicitation will not be issued. Telephone, email, and Fax requests for this solicitation will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. Amendments, if/when issued, will be posted to the website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors responsibility to check the website periodically for any amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System to for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right award to the next prospective Offeror. POINT-OF-CONTACT: The point-of-contact for this procurement is Contract Specialist, Mr. Seth Dukes at seth.j.dukes@usace.army.mil.

title: Multi-Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities on DDG-51 Class Ships Homeported in Norfolk, VA
description: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime (PAEM) is issuing solicitation N00024-26-R-4439 to procure a series of Multiple Ship Sustainment Partnership (MSSP) Single Award Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (SA-IDIQ) Contracts to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and Incremental Selected Restricted Availabilities (ISRAs) on DDG-51 Class ships homeported in Norfolk, VA. Fixed Price with Award Fees (FPAF) Contracts will be awarded across Facilitized and Non-Facilitized Lots. Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and CNO scheduled ISRAs, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities and ISRAs including, but not limited to, inter-availability preparation and administration (IAPA) support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all delivery orders for Fleet Maintenance Availabilities will be performed at the Government facility and all ISRAs will be performed in-plant at a Contactor-provided facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot on a full and open basis. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Non-Facilitized Lot includes Fleet Maintenance Availabilities only, to be completed on specific DDG-51 class ships that are not scheduled to complete ISRAs over the MSSP period of performance. The scope of this lot includes all efforts necessary to support continuous coordination, planning and preparation between contractor and government to complete Fleet Maintenance Availabilities including, but not limited to, IAPA support, inspections and assessments, engineering and design support, specification and other government furnished information reviews, and material procurement and logistics support. Unless otherwise specified in a Delivery Order Solicitation, all Delivery Orders will be performed at the Governments facility. The Navy will solicit this Lot as a Small Business Set Aside. The Navy intends to award up to three (3) Non-Facilitized Lot contracts. The number will be determined at contract award based on the number of acceptable proposals received. Each contract will include three (3) one-year ordering periods. The supply being procured is the repaired, mission-ready vessel, which is returned to service within the Fleet. This solicitation is issued electronically via PIEE and interested offerors should monitor PIEE and SAM.gov for any applicable solicitation amendments, thereafter. This posting does not include all relevant attachments. Potential offerors will need to request access to the attachments by providing a written request to the Contract Specialist, Alicia Vesey, at alicia.m.vesey.civ@us.navy.mil and the Contracting Officer, Paul Kang, at paul.k.kang.civ@us.navy.mil. title: Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry Art in Architecture
description: The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (Permanent Residents or Citizens of the United States of America ) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal facilities nationwide. GSA is announcing an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry in Brownsville, Texas. GSA is designing and constructing a new U.S. Land Port of Entry to replace the outdated Brownsville Gateway U.S. Land Port of Entry. The Land Port of Entry, once complete, will consist of multiple buildings for Federal inspection personnel who facilitate the transit of individuals and vehicles permitted entry into the United States from Mexico. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $550,000 to $800,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). Instructions on how to submit application materials and join the Registry are available on the following Web site: www.gsa.gov/real-estate/design-and-construction/art-in-architecturefine-arts/art-in-architecture-program/art-in-architecture-national-artist-registry All artists who wish to be considered as candidates for a commission at the U.S. Land Port of Entry in Brownsville, Texas, must have their application materials submitted and received by GSA by 5:00 PM Eastern Time, December 21, 2026. Artists� submissions received after the deadline will not be considered for this project but will be eligible for consideration on future GSA commissions alongside the other artists on the Registry. Artists already on the Registry need not resubmit but may elect to update their information prior to the deadline. GSA evaluates artists based on the following criteria: the media, materials, content and style of the artist�s past work, along with the artist�s past performance and experience with commissions or projects similar to the one described in this synopsis. Shortlisted artists will be contacted and asked to submit additional information, including a statement that the artist can perform the work associated with the GSA commission within the identified budget. GSA will count the combined weight of all the selection criteria as significantly more important than price. However, SAM registration is not needed at the time of submission of application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry. Instructions for creating an account and activating registration in SAM may be found at www.sam.gov. Artists selected for the contract award will be required to renew the registration in SAM on an annual basis for the duration of the project. In accordance with Executive Order 13934, Building and Rebuilding Monuments to American Heroes, GSA will prioritize the commission of works of art that portray historically significant Americans or events of American historical significance or illustrate the ideals upon which our Nation was founded.

description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 4 of 4 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 4 663A4-24-209 Replace Fire Suppression Systems Building 61 VA Puget Sound Medical Center - American Lake 9600 Veterans Drive Southwest, Lakewood, WA, 98439 Procurement Number: 36C26027R0008 This is a pre-solicitation notice synopsizing an upcoming competitive solicitation for a planned construction requirement. An invitation for Request for Proposals (RFP) is anticipated to be posted on or about November 2, 2026. The Veterans Affairs (VA) Puget Sound Medical Center-American Lake located in Lakewood, WA, has a requirement for a Firmed Fixed Price construction project to Replace Fire Suppression System to Building 61. Description of Services: Project Number 663A4-24-209 Replace Fire Suppression System to Building 61. Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, and equipment to replace the fire suppression systems at Building 61 in accordance with the associated and published/provided contract 100% Construction Documents (Drawings, Specifications, etc.). The Government requires the newly replaced systems to operate seamlessly with the existing systems at the American Lake campus. The replacement of the existing systems is to be performed within tolerance delineated in the Manufacturer's Installation Instructions. The new replacement packages will be submitted in accordance with the contract submittal process and approved by the Government prior to the Contractor proceeding with any part of the scope of work. Work includes all associated aspects, including but not limited to, cutting and patching, and repair of finishes. Removal and disposal of existing equipment, materials etc. Replacement of the dry-pipe sprinkler system in the attic, including connection to existing fire alarm system and new nitrogen generator Installation of the new fire alarm control panel 1st, 2nd & 3rd floor replacement of sprinkler heads and installation of new fire alarm system Connection of the new fire alarm system to campus monitoring Removal of the existing fire alarm system Installation of new fire alarm control panel in building 62. The magnitude of this project is between $1,000,000.00 and $5,000,000.00. Period of Performance: The intended contract period of performance is 365 calendar days after receipt of notice to proceed. NAICS Code: The NAICS Code is 238210 "Electrical Contractors and Other Wiring Installation Contractors", with a size standard of $19M. The solicitation will be issued as a request for proposals (RFP) under FAR part 15 procedures and in accordance with the updated Revolutionary FAR Overhaul. A bid bond is required, and the bid guarantee amount shall be at least 20 percent of the bid price but shall not exceed $3 million. This project is 100% set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses. All relevant solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings, may be accessed for download on the date of issue by conducting a search of Solicitation 36C26027R0008 on https://sam.gov/content/opportunities under Contract Opportunities. Any amendments to the presolicitation will be posted solely to this website. It is the responsibility of the offeror to verify the number of amendments issued. Prior to submitting an offer, (after solicitation is posted) all offerors must have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM): https://www.sam.gov/SAM/ with a fully completed Representations and Certifications Section and SDVOSB firms must be certified by the Small Business Administration: https://www.sba.gov/, to be eligible for a federal government contract award. The Government is accepting industry comments. Comments may or may not be incorporated, at the discretion of the Government. The Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Network Contracting Office 20 (NCO 20) anticipates making one (1) firm-fixed-price construction contract award based on a best value determination. An organized site visit is anticipated to be included in the details of the solicitation/RFP. All inquiries for this presolicitation shall be directed in writing to the NCO 20 Point of Contact- monique.king1@va.gov.

title: Switzerland – Electrical wiring and fitting work – RETROFIT DES CELLULES 6.4 kV DE JOULE PAR DE NOUVELLES CELLULES 24 KV SANS SF6
description: Le présent appel d'offres porte sur le renouvellement complet de l’installation moyenne tension (6,4 kV) du poste de Joule, situé au chemin du Bochet 5 ,1024 Ecublens et la fourniture de 32 nouvelles cellules MT conçues selon une technologie sans SF₆. Le projet s'inscrit dans la stratégie de modernisation du réseau de distribution de SIE SA et constitue une étape majeure de la migration progressive du réseau de distribution de 6,4 kV vers 21 kV. Le projet comprend notamment : * Le démontage, le recyclage et l'évacuation des cellules et matériel MT existantes ; * La démolition et l’évacuation des niches existantes ; * L’évacuation d’une bonbonne d’Azote présente dans le poste ; * L’élimination de 2 barils d’huile (416 l au total) ; * Le remplacement complet des cellules moyenne tension existantes ; * Le renouvellement des services auxiliaires AC et DC et des batteries ainsi que l’amélioration complète des installations CVSE ; * Le renouvellement des équipements de contrôle-commande, de protection et de communication ; * L'intégration des équipements existants conservés ; * Les travaux de génie civil nécessaires ; * Les adaptations des liaisons câblées moyenne tension existantes (optionnelle); * Le transport et montage de l’ensemble des équipements fournis ; * Les essais en usine (FAT), les essais sur site (SAT), les essais fonctionnels ainsi que la mise en service complète des installations ; * La remise de l'ensemble de la documentation conforme à l'exécution. Les nouvelles cellules devront permettre une exploitation dans une première phase sous une tension de 6,4 kV puis, sans modification structurelle des équipements principaux, sous une tension de 21 kV. En conséquent, les transformateurs de tension devront être dimensionnés pour permettre ce changement de tension modifications. Les cellules devront être conçues selon une technologie sans SF₆ et de préférence isolée à l’air et compatible avec les exigences environnementales actuelles et conformes aux prescriptions techniques du présent cahier des charges et des normes en vigueurs. Les équipements haute tension (50kV) existants ainsi que les transformateurs de puissance sont conservés. Le présent marché comprend uniquement les interfaces nécessaires à leur maintien en exploitation.

description: Le tronçon s’étend entre les Pk 69.250 et Pk 76.500, intégrant le tunnel de la Rochette, le tunnel de Pierre Pertuis, le tunnel de la Côte de Chaux, le tunnel Sous les Roches, la TC de la Métairie de Nidau et la TC de La Heutte. Les prestations du présent marché correspondent aux prestations (SIA MP, PP 32, 41, 51, 52, 53) d’auteur de projet (APR – Ingénieur GC) pour les secteurs TP4-TP5 à savoir le secteur Tavannes (y compris le tunnel de la Rochette) - La Heutte; La réalisation des phases de prestations du mandat concerne notamment les éléments suivants : · Mise en œuvre des nouveaux portiques, potences (11 emplacements), barres-tunnels, consoles et mâts comprenant l’analyse et la proposition du type de support, l’optimisation du positionnement, en relation avec les normes de signalisation et les équipements existants, le dimensionnement des nouvelles structures porteuses et de leurs fondations, la vérification des impacts sur les ouvrages et aménagements existants (viaducs, talus, etc.), ainsi que les raccordements nécessaires ; · Analyse et vérification/dimensionnement des portiques et potences existants ; · Analyse et vérification/dimensionnement des éléments de retenue au droit des portiques et potences existants et nouveaux ; · Les aspects GC liés aux nouvelles infrastructures en lien avec le BSA, telles que fouilles pour tous les raccordements BSA et de signalisation, y compris nouvelles chambres éventuelles ; · Remplacement et /ou assainissement des couvercles de gatics existants, y compris renouvellement des cadres en béton, et compléments éventuels nécessaires selon réévaluation en phase MP ; · Gestion de la dépose et de la remise en place des dallettes de caniveaux, y compris mises en dépôt provisoire et remplacements nécessaires ; · Coordination de la signalisation et des marquages provisoires en phases chantier pour les travaux de GC en collaboration avec les autres mandataires ; De réaliser les études pour les travaux GC nécessaire à l’APR BSA pour la réalisation de l’entretien et l'assainissement des installations BSA

title: Germany – Landscaping work – Grundinstandsetzung Behördenzentrum Platz der Luftbrücke 1 -3, 12101 Berlin. Herrichten Außenanlagen Hof 1-2 einschl. Leitungsgräben und baubegleitende Kampfmittelräumung (Vergabenummer O9611-e-003/26-097)
description: Das Behördenzentrum Platz der Luftbrücke (PdL) Columbiadamm 1-7c, Platz der Luftbrücke 1-3, Mehringdamm 129 und Schwiebusser Straße 129a-d in 12101 Berlin liegt im Stadtbezirk Tempelhof. Das Gesamtgebäude besteht aus elf miteinander verbundenen Bauteilen. Alle Bauteile verfügen über vier oberirdische Geschosse, ein nicht ausgebautes Dachgeschoss sowie ein bis teilw. zwei Untergeschoss(e). Das Behördenzentrum Platz der Luftbrücke wurde als Verwaltungskomplex zusammen mit dem benachbarten Flughafen Tempelhof nach den Plänen von Ernst Sagebiel für das Reichsluftfahrtministerium als sogenannter „Sonderbau“ in vier Bauabschnitten errichtet. Die Gebäude bilden ein Halbrund um den heute als „Platz der Luftbrücke“ bezeichneten Platz, der den Knotenpunkt der Ost-West- und Nord-Süd-Magistralen von Berlin bildet. Die Bauzeit des Behördenzentrums erstreckt sich ursprünglich auf die Jahre 1937 bis 1944. Nach 1945 wurden umfassende Reparaturen von Kriegsschäden, u.a. an Dächer und Fassaden durchgeführt. Die Bauteile VIII, IX und X wurden um 1955 einem umfassenden Neuaufbau unterzogen. Das Behördenzentrum Platz der Luftbrücke (PdL) steht unter Denkmalschutz und ist in die Denkmalliste Berlin, eingetragen (Eintragung am 06.04.1995, OBJ-Dok.-Nr. 09055092, Liste Tempelhof-Schöneberg). Das Behördenzentrum Platz der Luftbrücke (PdL) wird im Rahmen einer umfassenden konstruktiven, anlagenseitigen, energetischen und nutzungsspezifischen Grundinstandsetzung saniert. Bestandteil der im Leistungsverzeichnis beschriebenen Arbeiten ist die übergeordnete Baustelleneinrichtung und Baustellenlogistik für den sicheren und koordinierten Betrieb der Baustelle. Folgende Leistungen sind auszuführen: Das vorliegende Vergabeverfahren beinhaltet das Herrichten der Außenanlagen (nahezu 100 %iger Abbruch aller Beläge einschl. Unterbau), die Überprüfung luftbildsichtig kartierter konkreter Anhaltspunkte für das Vorhandensein von Kampfmitteln (Bombentrichter und Erdlöcher gemäß Räumkonzept durch Leistungen der ATV DIN 18323 Abschnitte 3.3, 3.4 und 3.6), die Herstellung von Leitungsgräben für die Leitungstrassen (großteils mit Verbau) jeweils einschließlich einer baubegleitenden Kampfmittelräumung gemäß Räumkonzept durch Leistungen der ATV DIN 18323 Abschnitt 3.8, das Schließen der Leitungsgräben nach bauseitiger Leitungsverlegung sowie das Andecken aller Flächen (mit Ausnahme des Baumbestandes) mit Recyclingschotter als Interimsparkplätze, sowie Baustelleneinrichtungsfläche für nachfolgende Hochbaumaßnahme im Zuge der Grundinstandsetzung des Behördenzentrums, Platz der Luftbrücke 1-3 in 12101 Berlin, Tempelhof. Die Ausschreibung beinhaltet folgende wesentliche Leistungen: - 5.250 m² Asphaltbelag abbrechen - 5.400 m² Betonfläche abbrechen - 2.435 m² Platten- und Pflasterbeläge abbrechen - 1.675 m Einfassungen, verschiedener Ausführung abbrechen - 170 Stück Ausstattungselemente u.a. Mastleuchten, Absperrpfosten, Fahrradbügel abbrechen - 1.500 m² Grasnarbe abschieben - 13.300 m² Schottertragschicht einbauen - 4.500 m³ Leitungsgräben, teilweise mit Verbau herstellen - 2 Stück Kampfmitteluntersuchung - Baubegleitende Kampfmitteluntersuchung für 16.450 m²

title: 25-153-A Nákup energetických setů
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je dodávka 30 kusů nových stejných elektrocentrál min. 80 kVA s kabelovým příslušenstvím, aretačním upevňovacím rámem a nářadím pro servis a opravy elektrocentrál (dále jen „EC“) a 12 kusů nových stejných samostatných přívěsných vozíků 3,5 t, (dále také „vozík 3,5 t“) včetně zajištění garančních prohlídek po celou dobu záruky za jakost dle čl. VIII kupní smlouvy (dále jen „garanční prohlídky“), a to pouze v případě, že budou ze strany dodavatele požadovány. Součástí dodávky je také zaškolení obsluhy, a to v rozsahu a za podmínek stanovených ve smlouvě.
