title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance
description: *Please note that the ISC website will be available on October 30th, 2026 as of 10:30am ET. This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en. Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/artificial-intelligence-ai-decision-making-process-visibility-traceability-and-compliance-governance Challenge title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) decision-making process visibility, traceability and compliance governance Challenge sponsor: Shared Services Canada (SSC) Funding Mechanism: Contract MAXIMUM CONTRACT VALUE: Multiple contracts could result from this Challenge. Phase 2: • The maximum funding available for any Phase 2 contract resulting from this Challenge is : $2,000,000.00 CAD excluding applicable taxes, shipping, travel and living expenses, as required. • The maximum duration for any Phase 2 contracts resulting from this Challenge is up to 20 months (excluding submission of the final report). • Estimated number of Phase 2 contracts: 1 This disclosure is made in good faith and does not commit Canada to award any contract for the total approximate funding. Final decisions on the number of Phase 1 and Phase 2 (amend as applicable) awards will be made by Canada on the basis of factors such as evaluation results, departmental priorities and availability of funds. Canada reserves the right to make partial awards and to negotiate project scope changes. Note: Selected companies are eligible to receive one contract per phase per challenge. Travel: No travel required. Kick-off Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Progress Review Meeting(s): Any progress review meetings will be conducted by telephone or videoconference. Final Review Meeting: All communication will take place by telephone or videoconference. Problem Statement: Challenge Statement Summary The Government of Canada (GoC) is committed to the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) compliant with its AI Strategy and Guiding Principles, see references noted in this challenge notice. The widespread adoption of AI technologies has created opportunities to enhance decision-making and improve service delivery within the GoC. In fostering the responsible usage of AI, the GoC has established an adoption strategy and guiding principles. To support adherence and implementation, the GoC is interested in testing solutions that provide visibility into AI decision-making processes, enhance the traceability of AI outputs, and ensure that AI models comply with Canadian laws and international standards and best practices. Despite the availability of AI governance solutions from Canadian companies and international providers, existing offerings typically require significant manual effort. This effort is particularly evident in interpreting evolving AI governance requirements, applying them to specific AI systems, updating controls and assessments, and identifying their ecosystem-wide impacts. The challenge seeks innovation to advance capabilities for identifying and incorporating evolving governance requirements, determining their potential impact on registered AI systems, associated controls, assessments, and evidence, and supporting timely reassessment, all while maintaining explainability, traceability, auditability, and human oversight. Details: Essential (mandatory) Outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Support the continuous alignment of registered AI systems with relevant Canadian regulations, policies, directives, and other governance requirements and be able to identify potentially affected systems and indicate when a reassessment is required. 2. Demonstrate interoperability with enterprise systems, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) platforms and governance solutions and the solution can be integrated with minimal customization. 2A. Demonstrate the ability to exchange governance information with enterprise systems and AI/ML lifecycle tools through standards-based Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), connectors and interoperable data exchange mechanisms. Governance information may include AI system metadata, risk assessments, compliance findings, audit evidence, monitoring results, approvals and decision records. As an example: This governance information includes but is not limited to, information about the AI system, ownership, intent, deployment status, funding state, client information, system objectives, assessments, algorithmic impact assessment, control requirements (playbooks). 2B. Demonstrate how governance information can be collected, aggregated and maintained across multiple systems through APIs, connectors and data exchange mechanisms. 2C. Leverage open standards and documented interfaces to reduce dependency on proprietary technologies enabling interoperability across diverse enterprise environments. 3. Demonstrate how administrative, support and access to governance information and data can be restricted, monitored and controlled in accordance with the GoC requirements. 3A. Enable organizations to define and manage data residency requirements, retention, access and deletion of policies and information without vendor intervention. 4. Enable assessment and reassessment of registered AI systems applicable AI governance requirements, policies, standards, directives while supporting reassessment when governance requirements, assessment frameworks are added modified, replaced or retired. The solution must demonstrate the ability to translate AI governance requirements into traceable controls assess whether applicable controls have been satisfied and identify non-conformities. 4A. Enable authorized users to add, modify, version, replace or retire governance requirements and assessment frameworks to individual AI systems or groups. Demonstrate compliance assessment at minimum against the Policy on Service and Digital, Directive on Automated Decision-Making, Algorithmic Impact Assessment, AI Strategy and AI ethics and responsibilities. 4B. Demonstrate the ability to add, modify, version, replace and retire governance requirements, controls and assessment criteria, and assign them to individual AI systems or groups of AI systems. while supporting the application of different assessment criteria to different AI systems based on their intended use, risk profile or governance requirements Offerors are encouraged to prove extensibility to additional internationally recognized governance frameworks and standards, including the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), International Organization for Standardization (ISO) and the EU Act. 4C. Generate human-readable explanations of assessment and reassessment results. Each finding must identify the applicable requirement, evidence considered, assessment result and confidence score or a certainty measure. user. 4D. Collect, link, and retain assurance artefacts including control mapping, assessment records, evidence references, approvals, exceptions, attestations, remediation actions and audit histories. The system must identify whether each artifact was provided by an authorised individual [Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)]. 4E. Provide measurable results and clearly distinguish between results when performing a compliance assessments to determine whether compliance is met, partially met, not

title: Albania – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Preparation of audits, detailed design, tender documents, supervision of civil works for the implementation of energy efficiency measures in local public buildings across all four municipalities
description: This Contract covers the preparation of investment-ready documentation for 50 pre-selected local public buildings in the municipalities of Berat, Shkodër, Korçë and Përmet, including offices, kindergartens, libraries, and social and cultural centres. The Assignment includes the preparation of energy audits, detailed technical designs, building permit documentation, Bills of Quantities, Environmental and Social Management Plans, and PRAG-compliant tender documentation. All 50 buildings will be assessed and prioritised in accordance with DCM No. 468/2024 . Based on this prioritisation, buildings with a total gross floor area of at least 22,000 m² will be selected for the implementation of energy-efficiency measures under a subsequent Works Contract. The Contract also includes the supervision of the civil works implemented in the selected buildings. The Service Contract is structured in two phases, comprising a total of 60 months of service provision, with a 12-month interim period between the two phases. Phase 1, lasting 24 months, covers the energy audit, preparation of the detailed technical design and preparation of the tender dossier for the Works Contract. This phase will be followed by a 12-month interim period, during which the procurement procedure for the Works Contract is expected to take place and no services will be required under the Service Contract. Phase 2, lasting 36 months, will cover the supervision and monitoring of the Works, commencing upon the start of the Works Contract.

title: Office of Hazardous Materials Safety Research Initiative � FY2026 BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA)
description: The U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT), Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA), Office of Hazardous Materials Safety (OHMS), is soliciting white papers and full proposals under Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) PHMSA-26HM-BAA pursuant to FAR 35.016. The objective of this announcement is to award competitive research contracts that advance scientific, technical, engineering, and policy solutions to prevent incidents and enhance safety during the transportation of hazardous materials across all modes. Offerors are invited to submit innovative research proposals addressing one or more of the following core topic areas: 26HM-ESS (Efficient Safety Standards): Research to modernize safety standards and testing, streamline certification, leverage safety data, and evaluate risk landscapes to reduce regulatory burden while maintaining safety. 26HM-SST (Safe Energy Storage Technologies): Research assessing transportation risks of energy storage systems, battery chemistries, thermal runaway detection and mitigation, and critical mineral recovery. 26HM-IPG (Innovative Packaging): Development and evaluation of advanced packaging materials, containment designs, integrity monitoring, and predictive failure simulations. 26HM-RER (Risk Reduction for Emergency Response): Innovations, technologies, data analysis, and materials to enhance emergency responder safety, communication, and preparedness. 26HM-RTS (Hazardous Materials Rail Transportation Safety): Research advancing scientific understanding of rail tank car performance under derailment conditions, crashworthiness materials, thermal shielding, and predictive risk modeling. A two-phase selection process (Phase I: White Paper; Phase II: Invited Full Proposal) will be used. Awards will be procurement contracts (Firm-Fixed-Price or Cost-Reimbursement) up to $2,000,000 with a total performance period of up to 36 months. title: Natchez Trace Parkway
description: Sealed bids from all business concerns will be accepted for the Pavement Rehabilitation Between MP 121 and MP 204 (Phase 3), Natchez Trace Parkway, Project MS NP NATR 3N19 3H28 ETC, Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000006, located in Attala, Choctaw, Leake, Madison, and Webster Counties, Mississippi. The work includes full depth reclamation, pavement patching, milling, asphalt overlay, pavement marking, signing, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $60,000,000 to $70,000,000. Please Note the apparent successful bidder is required to submit a Project Labor Agreement (PLA) prior to contract award pursuant to FAR Provision 52.222-33, Alternate I and FAR Clause 52.222-34. The PLA must meet the requirements of Executive Order 14063 and the policies and procedures of FAR Subpart 22.5 - Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 20, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. IMPORTANT SUBCONTRACTING PLAN REQUIREMENTS Required from all "other than small business" when the requirement is expected to exceed $900,000 ($2,000,000 for construction) [FAR 19.109]. Contracting Officer, Contracting Officer�s Representative, and Small Business Specialist are responsible for approving a reasonable and realistic plan [FAR 19.206-3] [TAM 1219.201(e)(6)]. Legislated subcontracting goals are 40.13% - Small Businesses (SB), 5% - Small Disadvantaged Businesses (SDB), 5% - Women-Owned Small Business Entities (WOSB), 3% - HUBZone, 5% - Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). A copy of each subcontracting plan (or contractor statement that no subcontracts are to be awarded) must be provided to Eastern Federal Lands and approved by the Office of Small Disadvantaged Business Utilization prior to close of negotiations (or award of the IFB) [TAM 1219.705-5 and -6]. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. title: Sources Sought for (ICP-OES) Spectrometer System with an Autosampler
description: The Request for Information (RFI) in anticipation of under NAICS 334516, Subject to FAR Clause 52-213 entitled Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes, this announcement constitutes a Request for Information for written information only. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. This is a Request for Information (RFI) in anticipation of a potential future procurement program under NAICS code 334516. Subject to FAR Clause 52.215-3, entitled Request for Information or Solicitation for Planning Purposes, this announcement constitutes a Request for Information for written information only. The Naval Supply System Command (NAVSUP), Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk (FLCN) is conducting market research to remain competitive in an increasingly competitive world. In accordance with Title 10 of US Code, the United States Naval Academy has a mandate to admit qualified applicants from every congressional district in the United States. As a result of this mandate, our outreach and marketing efforts have a national focus, and also include territories outside of the continental United States. The Office of Admissions seeks to leverage channels that support outreach activities nationwide via conversational software. The Support required under this anticipated procurement is included in the draft Statement of Work (SOW) provided with this notice. RFI SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS: Interested parties shall submit responses to this RFI. Responses should reference the RFI and shall include the following information in this format: 1. Company name, address, Point of Contact name, phone number, and email address. 2. Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code and DUNS Number. 3. Business size under NAICS. 4. Describe your ability to support the scope of the requirement listed in this notice and applicable attachments. 5. Describe any past performance efforts with a similar scope to the proposed requirement. Provide contract numbers, dollar value, and the period of performance for each contract referenced in the response to this sources sought notice. 6. Indicate if your company can be a prime contractor for this effort or, if not, whether your company can be a subcontractor. If subcontractors are to be used, provide the anticipated percentage of effort to be subcontracted and if a small or large businesses will be used. This announcement is NOT a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the U.S. Government. The Navy will not assume liability for costs incurred in response to this RFI. Documentation of technical expertise and experience must be presented in sufficient detail for the U.S. Government to determine that your company possesses the necessary functional area expertise and experience to compete for this acquisition. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submissions are not to exceed five (5) typewritten pages in no less than 12 font. All technical questions and inquiries may be submitted within the response. Responses should be emailed to Shere' C. Reese at shere.c.reese.civ@us.navy.mil by 2:00 pm Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 22 December 2025. Again, this is not a request for a proposal. Respondents will not be notified of the results and the U.S. Government is not required to answer any questions submitted in regards to this RFI. Please note the information within this pre-solicitation synopsis will be updated and/or may change prior to an official synopsis/solicitation, if any. No phone calls will be accepted.

INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Respondents should address the capability areas and information requested in this RFI without assuming any relationship to that program�s requirements, acquisition approach, funding, schedule, or procurement quantities. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. These capabilities may enable operators to safely practice in realistic and challenging operational and threat environments, emergency procedures, and degraded system behaviors that may be impractical, unsafe, or cost-prohibitive to execute using live aircraft. Simulation-based training may also reduce operational impacts associated with range availability, airspace restrictions, spectrum congestion, weather delays, aircraft maintenance requirements, and logistical constraints while supporting standardized, repeatable, and scalable training across multiple UAS platforms. The Government seeks to understand current industry capabilities, technology maturity, innovative approaches, best practices, and limitations relevant to these objectives. MARKET RESEARCH PROCESS This RFI represents the white-paper phase of Air PMO's market research effort. The Government may use information received to support capability development, requirements refinement, acquisition planning, evaluation of commercially available and emerging solutions, and potential procurement strategies. Following review of submitted white papers, the Government may invite selected respondents to participate in follow-up discussions or technical demonstrations to further assess the maturity, suitability, and applicability of proposed solutions. Selection for, or participation in, a follow-up activity does not constitute a competitive range determination, source-selection decision, commitment to procure, or preference for any future acquisition. Any invitation and associated instructions will be issued separately. The Government may elect not to conduct follow-up activities and is not obligated to provide feedback to respondents. INFORMATION REQUESTED Respondents should provide a concise white paper describing how their solution addresses the capability areas in this RFI. Responses should identify current capabilities separately from planned, developmental, or partner-provided capabilities. At a minimum, the white paper should address the following: Company profile, business size and socioeconomic status, Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and primary point(s) of contact. Executive summary of the proposed solution and the operational or training problem it addresses. Description of the complete solution, including software, hardware, peripherals, hosting or deployment model, licensing, and any Government-furnished equipment or services required. A capability cross-reference identifying each applicable Capability Area of Interest as currently available, configurable, developmental, not available, or provided by a third party. For developmental capabilities, identify the anticipated availability date and key dependencies. Supported Group 1 and Group 2 UAS platforms, flight models, ground control stations, hand controllers, payloads, mission-planning tools, and training environments, including the approach and estimated effort to add new aircraft or configurations. Technical maturity and commercial availability, including Technology Readiness Level or equivalent maturity evidence, operational use, customer base, relevant contracts, and available test or performance data. System architecture, interfaces, data formats, application programming interfaces, standards, modularity, and approach to integration with Government or third-party systems. Training-management, instructor, evaluation, after-action review, records-management, and qualification-management functionality. Cybersecurity, identity and access management, data protection, software-update, cloud or on-premises deployment, and authority-to-operate status or experience, as applicable. NDAA and supply-chain compliance status, including identification of any noncompliant components, planned remediation, dependencies, or assumptions. Implementation approach, schedule, lead times, training and support model, sustainment, warranties, upgrades, and product roadmap. title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. Site Visit Registration Registration is required to attend the site visit. To register, contact Nicole Williams, Concessions Management Specialist, Lake Mead National Recreation Area at nicole_williams@nps.gov, along with a courtesy copy to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov, no later than 12:00 pm (Pacific Time) on September 17, 2026. You must provide your name, contact information, the name of the entity interested in submitting a proposal that you represent, the primary contact for the entity, and the number and names of people in your party. Due to space constraints, the NPS limits the number of site visit attendees to a total of five (5) people per interested entity. Site visit participants are responsible for obtaining their lodging, meals, and transportation to the Concession Facilities. The operation is located at 490 Horsepower Cove, Boulder City, NV 89005. Attendance at the site visit is encouraged, but not required, to submit a proposal. The NPS will not answer questions about this prospectus or business opportunity during registration or the site visit. Interested entities must submit questions in writing after the release of the prospectus to the contact person and by the deadline that will be provided in the prospectus. Interested entities are asked not to interfere with concessioner operations during the site visit and not to film, record or photograph concessioner employees or concessioner operations. Questions Due Questions regarding the prospectus must be received, in writing, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on September 30, 2026. Email your questions to Mark Juretschke, Commercial Services Program, National Park Service, Interior Regions 8, 9, 10, and 12, at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov. Notice of Intent to Propose Any interested party intending to submit a proposal must submit a "Notice of Intent to Propose" as described in the Business Opportunity and Proposal Instructions, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on November 23, 2026. Submission of Electronic Proposal The NPS is ONLY accepting electronic proposals in response to this prospectus. Any proposal must be received electronically, no later than 12:00 p.m. (Pacific Time) on December 22, 2026, in the format outlined in the Proposal Instructions, to be evaluated for award of the new concession contract. Contact List The prospectus is available on the NPS Commercial Services website (link provided below). If you choose to retrieve a copy of the prospectus, please notify Mark Juretschke at PWR_Commercial_Services@nps.gov so you are placed on the mailing list to receive notifications of any future modifications or correspondence.

title: Beach Renourishment, Kennedy Space Center, Brevard County, Florida
description: This announcement constitutes a Source Sought Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The Jacksonville District of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking interest from prospective offerors for a potential fiscal year (FY) 2027 award of the aforementioned project. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to gauge of interest, capabilities and qualifications of various members of the Construction and Dredging Communities, to include Small Businesses, as the Government must ensure there is adequate competition amongst the potential pool of responsible contractors. The notice is also soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for this large-scale construction project exceeding $35,000,000. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said notice or any follow-up information requested. The proposed project will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract. The Jacksonville District anticipates the issuance of an Invitation For Bid (IFB). No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to said sources sought notice or any follow-up information requested. DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The proposed project work will consist of nourishing approximately 4.1 miles shoreline along Kennedy Space Center between FDEP Range Monuments V-366 and V-386 in Brevard County, Florida. The project includes dredging approximately 2.5 million cubic yards (MCY) of material for construction of a beach berm and dune. Beach compatible sand for the project may be dredged from up to three (3) offshore borrow areas. Chester Shoals I is located east of Cape Canaveral in State waters and is centered approximately 1.7 miles offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Kennedy Shoals and Hetzel Shoals are located east of Cape Canaveral in Federal waters and are centered approximately 4.5 miles and 10 miles, respectively, offshore of Kennedy Space Center. Project work also includes, but is not limited to, beach tilling, turbidity monitoring, environmental species monitoring, and Munitions and Explosive of Concern (MEC) support. The project will have an estimated period of performance of 280 calendar days after issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP), including 60 calendar days to commence work. Magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The NAICS Code is 237990 Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the SMALL BUSINESS STANDARD SIZE IS $45,000,000.00. Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about June 1, 2027 and the anticipated bid opening day is on or about July 1, 2027. The official Synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on the SAM.gov Contracting Opportunities Website: www.sam.gov. An Invitation for Bid will be issued in electronic format only and will be posted on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://www.sam.gov/. Please be advised, if you are not registered, the Government is not responsible for providing you with notification to any changes to this solicitation. Do you have knowledge that Project Labor Agreement (PLA) has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation? 8. Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. NOTES: DO NOT SUBMIT A RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE IF YOU DO NOT INTEND TO BID ON THIS PROJECT. DO NOT SUBMIT PROPRIETARY AND/OR BUSINESS CONFIDENITAL DATA. Submission Instructions: Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the work associated with the subject requirement, are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice no later than December 22, 2026 at 5:00PM, local time. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice shall be sent to Mrs. Ruth Rodriquez via email at ruth.c.rodriguez@usace.army.mil and Mr. Guesley Leger at guesley.leger@usace.army.mil. title: Netherlands – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – DAS SURF Cumulus Professional Services 2023
description: De toekomst van de ICT en bijbehorende dienstverlening voor onderwijs- en onderzoek ligt volgens SURF én de leden voor een belangrijk deel in de cloud. De leden (instellingen) willen daarom flexibel gebruik kunnen maken van de cloud en deze combineren met eigen ICT-infrastructuren (hybride infrastructuur). Overgang naar de cloud is in de praktijk geen eenvoudige stap, en voor veel instellingen geldt dat er weinig ervaring mee is opgedaan. Er kunnen daardoor onverwachte uitdagingen ontstaan tijdens de uitvoering van cloud projecten alsook in de beheerfase erna. De initieel beoogde voordelen worden dan niet behaald waardoor afbreukrisico c.q. kapitaalvernietiging kan ontstaan. Om instellingen te ondersteunen bij deze uitdagingen is het dan ook gewenst om SURFcumulus Professional Services via een SURF aanbesteding voor hen beschikbaar te maken. SURF kiest ervoor om dit via een DAS te laten verlopen. De levering van SURFcumulus Professional Services is nadrukkelijk gekoppeld aan de SURFcumulus dienst. Concreet gaat het om uitvoerende, gangbare dienstverlening bedoeld voor cloud implementatie, -migratie en -beheer. Levering gebeurt op basis van vaste prijs en vaste opleverdatum. Een nadere omschrijving van de dienstverleningonderdelen is als volgt: Inrichten van een cloud landing zone, geïntegreerd in de bestaande (hybride) architectuur van een instelling, ten minste omvattend: Account setup: gebaseerd op de administratieve organsiatie, compliance richtlijnen, bestaande omgevingen en structuren van de instelling. Network configuratie: volgens richtlijnen, binnen cloud omgevingen en tussen on-premise en deze cloud omgevingen. Security baseline: identity en access management op basis van SURFconext, bechikbaarheid van gestandaardiseerde, hardened machine images, security policies, network monitoring en log analytics. Automation: gestandaardiseerde inrichting van security, governance, and kostenoptimalisatie. Uitvoeren/ondersteunen van cloud migraties, door middel van: Lift-and-shift migratie scenario: het zonder ingrijpende wijzigingen (deels) verplaatsen van een ICT infrastructuur uit een datacenter naar de cloud. Re-design migratie scenario: het cloud ready maken van (een deel van) een bestaande ICT infrastructuur en/of het implementeren van vervangende, nieuw te bouwen oplossingen waardoor het potentieel van de cloud optimaal benut kan worden. Leveren van cloud managed services in de (hybride) cloud infrastructuur, waaronder bijv.: Operations (accountbeheer, software update management, licentiebeheer, netwerkbeheer, backup & restore, monitoring, platformbeheer) Application management (technisch applicatiebeheer, functioneel applicatiebeheer, gegevensbeheer, applicatie configuratiebeheer) Service support (incident-, problem- & change management, multi vendor coordinatie, tweede en derdelijns support, escalatie afhandeling) Service delivery (service level management, capacity-, cost- en continuity management) Informatie beveiliging en privacy bescherming (detectie, preventie, rapportage, bijsturing). Zie verder het toegevoegde document "Toelatingsleidraad DAS SURFcumulus Professional Services".

title: Maximum Length Sequence Phase Encoding for Quantum Sensor Readout
description: Quantum sensors can detect extremely small electromagnetic and magnetic signatures, which makes them powerful tools for geophysical analysis, materials detection, environmental monitoring, and scientific research. Their sensitivity also makes them vulnerable to interference from ambient RF sources, electrical noise, and outdoor or industrial environments. Traditional readout methods attempt to preserve the phase of the sensor or allow it to evolve uniformly, but these approaches can produce ambiguous results or false positives when exposed to strong interference. Los Alamos researchers developed a pseudorandom phase-encoding method that allows a quantum sensor to distinguish true target signals from substantial background noise. By applying a maximum length sequence, also called an msequence, the sensor�s phase is flipped by 180 degrees according to a designed pattern. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation
description: Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation from scientists at Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a cleaner, flexible way to capture and concentrate rare earth elements from complex liquid mixtures by using a bio-inspired protein system that gathers target metals into separable clusters. The approach is designed to reduce reliance on harsher processing methods while supporting more resilient supply chains for critical materials used across energy, electronics, transportation and advanced manufacturing markets. Because the system is genetically modular, the same platform may be adapted with different Lanmodulin-type metal-binding variants to support selective capture needs across varied feedstocks. How it Works The technology modifies Lanmodulin, a protein known for strong rare earth element binding, by adding an �encapsulation peptide" to the N-terminus of the protein. Once the engineered protein binds rare earth elements in solution, the resulting protein-metal complexes can be triggered for self-assemble into biomolecular condensates, which are larger clusters that can be removed from the liquid. The material can then be separated and concentrated through various means�such as centrifugation, filtration, and sedimentation�reducing the need for immobilizing the protein on a column or other fixed support. Technical Description Rare earth elements are important to modern technologies; yet, processing and purification can be difficult and environmentally damaging. Protein-Based Rare Earth Recovery via Condensation addresses that problem through EP-LanM, an engineered version of Lanmodulin that changes its material state when rare earth elements are present. Rather than focusing only on changing which rare earth elements Lanmodulin binds, this technology changes how the protein behaves after binding, turning dissolved protein-metal complexes into recoverable droplets. The metals can be harvested from the protein droplets, and the resultant free-protein itself can be recycled into iterative separations. The protein architecture is modular, with the encapsulation peptide fused to Lanmodulin so the protein can self-assemble in response to rare earth element binding. The assembled EP-LanM-rare earth complexes can be captured through simple centrifugation, filtration, or sedimentation, which may simplify processing compared with approaches that require immobilization on a column. The modular design may also support use with other Lanmodulin derivatives that have been designed for specific rare earth affinities, creating a path toward tailored separation strategies � without requiring a full redesign of the recovery concept. title: Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA Facility)
description: An accelerator-driven, sub-critical molten-salt nuclear system that centrally produces large quantities of tritium for fusion energy. By pairing accelerator-driven subcritical operation with molten-salt chemistry, the system offers a controllable, safety-forward pathway to produce fusion fuel, recover useful energy and convert legacy nuclear liabilities into strategic energy assets. Overview: The Accelerator-Driven Sub-Critical Molten-Salt Assembly (ADS+MSA) is a centralized nuclear facility that uses a high-power particle accelerator coupled to a liquid molten-salt system to reliably produce kilogram-scale quantities of tritium. Because the system is sub-critical, nuclear reactions only occur when driven by the accelerator, providing inherent safety and operational control. By combining proven accelerator technology with modern molten-salt chemistry, the ADS+MSA removes a major bottleneck to commercial fusion energy, recovers useful energy, and strengthens U.S. energy security and national security missions under existing Department of Energy safety frameworks rather than commercial reactor licensing. Key Advantages: Enables large-scale commercial fusion energy by providing a reliable, centralized source of tritium, eliminating the need for fusion plants to breed their own fuel and significantly reducing cost, complexity, and deployment risk. Operates in an inherently safe, sub-critical configuration in which nuclear reactions stop when the accelerator is turned off, avoiding runaway scenarios and allowing operation under DOE accelerator safety orders rather than NRC power-reactor licensing. Achieves extremely high tritium production efficiency, with tritium breeding ratios far exceeding those achievable in fusion reactor blankets, enabling kilogram-scale production with substantially lower accelerator power than earlier accelerator-only concepts. Builds on decades of proven accelerator development and growing industrial experience with molten-salt systems, reducing technical risk and enabling modular, scalable deployment as demand increases. title: France – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Etude des schémas directeurs eaux usées et eaux pluviales Secteur 4
description: Le contrat porte sur les prestations suivantes : ETUDE DES SCHEMAS DIRECTEURS EAUX USEES ET EAUX PLUVIALES - SECTEUR 4 : La Plaine, La Romagne, Le Voide, Les Cerqueux, Nueil-sur-Layon, Saint-Hilaire-du-Bois, Saint-Léger-sous-Cholet, Somloire, Vihiers, Maulévrier Cholet Agglomération souhaite répondre aux enjeux et objectifs suivants : • évaluer la mise en œuvre des précédents schémas directeurs, en particulier sur le volet eaux usées, • atteindre 100 % de conformité des systèmes d’assainissement, • accompagner les projections d’urbanisation et d’aménagement du territoire traduites dans les zonages et le PLUi-H adopté en février 2026, • structurer et adapter la gestion des eaux pluviales urbaines dans une perspective durable et intégrée, • garantir la protection du milieu naturel, • anticiper l’évolution de la réglementation DERU 2 et du SDAGE 2028/2032, • disposer d’outils de gestions technique et économique du patrimoine qui définissent la planification des investissements et un programme précis de travaux à l’échelle intercommunale. Ainsi, l’étude s’appuiera sur les schémas directeurs précédents pour bâtir un nouveau plan pluriannuel d’investissement, à horizon 10 ans minimum, permettant de garantir le bon état de son patrimoine et son adéquation avec les évolutions urbaines, démographiques et économiques du territoire communautaire, ainsi que le respect des exigences réglementaires, la protection des milieux récepteurs, des biens et des personnes. A titre prévisionnel, les prestations devraient débuter en mars 2027, pour une durée maximum de 22 mois. Le marché est décomposé en 4 phases pour le schéma directeur eaux usées et 1 phase pour le schéma directeur eaux pluviales, définies comme suit : Schéma directeur eaux usées : Phase I : Etat des lieux et pré-diagnostic, Phase II : Recherche et caractérisation des eaux claires parasites et des surverses, Phase III : Modélisation, prospective, Phase IV : Bilan récapitulatif, étude de scénarios et élaboration du schéma directeur, Schéma directeur eaux pluviales : Phase I : Actualisation du bilan patrimonial et de la connaissance des dysfonctionnements. Durée Le marché prend effet à sa notification, et s'achève à l'issue de la dernière phase. Le délai d'exécution maximum du marché fixé par le maître d'ouvrage pour l’ensemble des phases est de 22 mois, hors période de validation.
